etymologies.etymologyHTML: From disclose by analogy with closure. A purely English formation.

quote.citation: 1815 December (indicated as 1816), [Jane Austen], chapter 13, in Emma: […], volume III, London:  […]  [Charles Roworth and James Moyes] for John Murray, →OCLC:
quote.text: Seldom, very seldom, does complete truth belong to any human disclosure; seldom can it happen that something is not a little disguised, or a little mistaken;  […]

definitions.definition: (law) The making known of a previously hidden fact or series of facts to another party; the act of disclosing.
That which is disclosed; a previously hidden fact or series of facts that is made known.
